history.summary: RELATED TO SEQ 1697 (Murudeshwara Temple) - this CSV row covers the Ganapathi and Subramaniyar sub-shrines inside the Murudeshwara Temple complex on Kanduka Hill, not a separate standalone temple. A separate Ganesha shrine within the complex is documented by travel sources: a sculpted Ganesha idol visited for blessings of prosperity, success and removal of obstacles. A dedicated Subramaniyar (Kartikeya) shrine is NOT individually documented in the web sources consulted - UNVERIFIED; it may be a minor sannidhi within the modern complex. Timings, travel and history otherwise follow the main Murudeshwara Temple (seq 1697). No sub-shrine-specific photograph was found after genuine searching, so the media image shows the temple complex.

name: Ganapathi and Subramaniyar Sub-shrines, Murudeshwara Temple Complex
town_description: Murudeshwar (Murudeshwara) is a coastal town in Bhatkal taluk of Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka, on the Arabian Sea coast along NH-66, about 155-165 km south of Mangaluru. Built on and around the Kanduka Hill, which juts into the sea on three sides, it is both a major Shiva pilgrimage centre and a beach tourism destination, and lies on the Konkan Railway line.

travel.road: Within the Murudeshwara Temple complex on Kanduka Hill, Murudeshwar, on NH-66.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Follow the main temple's hours (verify): 6:00 AM-1:00 PM and 3:00-8:00 PM
